9830               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9831               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9832               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9833               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9834               	; 	' runs every pass.
9835               	; 	'
9836               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9837               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9838               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9839               	; 	'
9840               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9841               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9842               	; 	'
9843               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9844               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9845               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
9846               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
9847               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
9848               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
9849               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
9850               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
9851               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
9852               	; 	'
9853               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
9854               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
9855               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
9856               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
9857               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a
9858               	; 	' speed ratio of 2.0 leaves the on-foot chase 0.2 s of slack, which is no
9859               	; 	' chase at all. checkchase.py holds the line.
9860               	; 	' STILL RUNNING FROM THE STAIRS -- and this has to come BEFORE the move,
9861               	; 	' not after it. It sat below the two `IF hmv` blocks, where all it could
9862               	; 	' still reach was the animation counter: he faced the right way, played
9863               	; 	' the run cycle and did not travel a pixel. He stood at the foot of the

9866               	; 	' TWO THINGS END THE RUN, AND BOTH ARE VISIBLE ON SCREEN.

9961               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9962               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9963               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9964               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
9965               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
9966               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
9967               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
9968               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9969               	; 	'
9970               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
9971               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
9972               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
9973               	; 	'
9974               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
9975               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
9976               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
9977               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
9978               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
9979               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
9980               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
9981               	; 	'
9982               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
9983               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
9984               	; 	'
9985               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
9986               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
9987               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
9988               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
9989               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
9990               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
9991               	; 	'
9992               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
9993               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
9994               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
9995               	; 	' before any of this.
9996               	; 	'
9997               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
9998               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
9999               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the
10000               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his
10001               	; 	' journey.
10002               	; 	'
10003               	; 	' `hanim` still advances by hspd and is still an ODOMETER -- pixels
10004               	; 	' travelled, not time -- so the run cycle stays locked to the ground at any
10005               	; 	' rate. A 9 px step moves it exactly one pose of its 8 px beat.

10466               	;
10467               	; 	' ======================================================================
10468               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10469               	; 	' ======================================================================
10470               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10471               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10472               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10473               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10474               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10475               	; 	'
10476               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10477               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10478               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10479               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10480               	; 	' broken.
10481               	; 	'
10482               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10483               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10484               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10485               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10486               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10487               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10488               	; 	'
10489               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10490               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10491               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10492               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10493               	; coll_obst:
10494               cvb_COLL_OBST

     E2B4 219C     
10815               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10816               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10817               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10818               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10819               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10820               	; 	' away from.
10821               	; 	'
10822               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10823               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10824               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10825               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10826               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10827               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10828               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10829               	; 	'
10830               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10831               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10832               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10833               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10834               	; 	'
10835               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10836               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10837               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10838               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10839               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10840               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10841               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10842               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10843               	; 	'
10844               	; 	' A ducking Kop is still stood up, because the crouch is a held pose and
10845               	; 	' there is nothing to interrupt.

11004               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
11005               	; 	'
11006               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
11007               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
11008               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
11009               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
11010               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
11011               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
11012               	; 	'
11013               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
11014               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
11015               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
11016               	; 	'
11017               	; 	' UNSIGNED-SAFE. Riding up is above the shared floor and riding down is
11018               	; 	' below it, which is a signed quantity, and CVBasic's variables are not.
11019               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
11020               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
11021               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
11022               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of
11023               	; 	' their heights, which is exactly the distance between them.

11135               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
11136               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three

12261               	; 	' ======================================================================
12262               	; 	' THE SCANNER
12263               	; 	' ======================================================================
12264               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12265               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12266               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12267               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12268               	; 	'
12269               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12270               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12271               	; 	'
12272               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12273               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12274               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12275               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12276               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12277               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12278               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
12279               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
12280               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12281               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
12282               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
12283               	; esc_tick:
12284               cvb_ESC_TICK
12285               	; 	' ONLY SCREENS 0 AND 7 CARRY A FLIGHT, so six screens in eight skip this
12286               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
12287               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
12288               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12289               	; 	IF klsc > 0 THEN
12290 ED84 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLSC,r0
     ED86 21AC     
12291 ED88 0201  20 	li r1,256   ; 1*256
     ED8A 0100     
12292 ED8C 9040  18 	cb r0,r1
12293 ED8E 1402  14 	jhe cv836
12294 ED90 0460  28 	b @cv835
     ED92 EDA8     
12295               cv836
12296               	; 		IF klsc < 7 THEN RETURN
12297 ED94 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLSC,r0
     ED96 21AC     
12298 ED98 0201  20 	li r1,1792   ; 7*256

12308               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
12309               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12310               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12311               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12312               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12313               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12314               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12315               	; 	'
12316               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12317               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12318               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12319               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12320               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12321               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
12322               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.
12323               	; 	escp = escp + 1

12619               	;
12620               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12621               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12622               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12623               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12624               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12625               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12626               	; 	'
12627               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12628               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12629               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12630               	; 	'
12631               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12632               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12633               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12634               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12635               	; 	'
12636               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12637               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12638               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12639               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12640               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12641               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12642               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12643               	; 	'
12644               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12645               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12646               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12647               	; 	'
12648               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12649               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why
12650               	; 	' scan_escs and scan_elev redraw every tick rather than once.
12651               	; scan_furn:
12652               cvb_SCAN_FURN

12992               	;
12993               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
12994               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
12995               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
12996               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
12997               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
12998               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12999               	; scan_wipe:
13000               cvb_SCAN_WIPE
13001               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
13002               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
13003               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
13004               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
13005               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
13006               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
13007               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
13008               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
13009               	; 	'
13010               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
13011               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
13012               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
13013               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
13014               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
13015               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
13016               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
13017               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
13018               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
13019               	; 	'
13020               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
13021               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
13022               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
13023               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
13024               	; 	'
13025               	; 	' renumber.py rewrites this line from genart.SCAN_FIRST, and
13026               	; 	' checkstruct.py fails the build if the two disagree.
13027               	; 	#swa = 5760			' 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8, the canvas patterns
13028 F29C 0200  20 	li r0,5760
     F29E 1680     
13029 F2A0 C800  38 	mov r0,@cvb__SWA
     F2A2 20EC

13095               	;
13096               	; 	' THE TWO ACTORS ARE SPRITES; EVERYTHING ELSE IS CHARACTERS.
13097               	; 	'
13098               	; 	' That split is what makes the instrument simple. The floor lines, the
13099               	; 	' flights and the lift car do not move relative to the canvas, so they
13100               	; 	' are pixels in the scanner's own characters and cost nothing to keep.
13101               	; 	' The Kop and the crook DO move, and as sprites they need no colour
13102               	; 	' table, no erase and no priority arithmetic -- they draw over the
13103               	; 	' furniture because sprites always do, and nothing shifts to make room.
13104               	; 	'
13105               	; 	' IT ALSO REMOVED THE BLINK. Kelly flashed because a pixel row of this
13106               	; 	' canvas can only carry one colour, so at close range the two markers
13107               	; 	' merged and the blink was the only thing left to tell them apart. Two
13108               	; 	' sprites are two colours wherever they stand.
13109               	; 	'
13110               	; 	' The furniture is drawn ONCE, by scan_furn. It used to be redrawn every
13111               	; 	' tick because erasing a character-based marker ANDed bits out of
13112               	; 	' whatever it was standing on; there is nothing left to rub it away. The
13113               	; 	' car still redraws itself, because the car actually moves.
13114               	; 	' -- the lift car. IT WAS FLICKERING, and the cause was not the drawing
13115               	; 	' but the ERASING: scan_elev cleared its three cells and put them back
13116               	; 	' every tick, whether or not the car had moved, so several times a second
13117               	; 	' there was a window with the pixels off. A sprite has no erase at all --
13118               	; 	' it is placed, and the VDP does the rest -- and slot 26 sits BELOW the
13119               	; 	' two markers, so the Kop and the crook pass over it without either of

13904               	;
13905               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13906               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13907               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13908               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13909               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13910               	; 	'
13911               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13912               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13913               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13914               	; 	'
13915               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13916               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13917               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13918               	; 	'
13919               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
13920               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
13921               	; 	'
13922               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
13923               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
13924               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
13925               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
13926               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
13927               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
13928               	; 	'
13929               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
13930               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
13931               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
13932               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
13933               	; 	'
13934               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
13935               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
13936               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
13937               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)
13938               	; bonus_count:
13939               cvb_BONUS_COUNT

14054               	;
14055               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
14056               	; 	'
14057               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
14058               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
14059               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
14060               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
14061               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
14062               	; 	'
14063               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
14064               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
14065               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
14066               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
14067               	; 	' counting stops.
14068               	;
14069               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
14070               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
14071               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
14072               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
14073               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
14074               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
14075               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
14076               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
14077               	; 	'
14078               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
14079               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
14080               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).

14236               	; 	' Silence every channel FIRST. SOUND latches, and the per-channel decay

14682               	;
14683               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14684               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14685               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14686               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14687               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14688               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14689               	;
14690               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14691               	; 	'
14692               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14693               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14694               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14695               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14696               	; 	'
14697               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14698               	; 	'
14699               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14700               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14701               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14702               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14703               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14704               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14705               	; 	'
14706               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14707               	; 	'
14708               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14709               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14710               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14711               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14712               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14713               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14714               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14715               	; 	'
14716               	; 	' 104 px/s over 15 px is 6.9 a second -- between the 8.0 that read as
14717               	; 	' slightly hurried and the 6.1 that read as trudging. The dial is this one
14718               	; 	' constant and the subtraction below, which must stay threshold + 1 or the
14719               	; 	' carry is wrong.
14720               	; 	'
14721               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14722               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14723               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14724               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14725               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14726               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14727               	; 	'
14728               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14729               	; 	'
14730               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14731               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14732               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14733               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14734               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14735               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not
14736               	; 	' back to 7.

14860               	;
14861               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14862               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14863               	; 	'
14864               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14865               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14866               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14867               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14868               	; 	'
14869               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14870               	; 	'
14871               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14872               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14873               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14874               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14875               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14876               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14877               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14878               	; 	'
14879               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14880               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14881               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14882               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14883               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
14884               	; 	'
14885               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
14886               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
14887               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
14888               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
14889               	; 	#if TI994A
14890               	; 	BANK 2
14891      00FE     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$
     **** ****     > .rept

15555               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15556               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15557               	; 	'
15558               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15559               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15560               	; 	' being small sprites.
15561               	; 	'
15562               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15563               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15564               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15565               	; 	'
15566               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15567               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15568               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15569               	;
15570               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15571               cvb_SPR_KELLY

16701               	; 	' -------------------------------------------------- scanner canvas
16702               	; 	' Chars 208-255: 16 cols x 3 rows over screen rows 21-23. Blank to start;
16703               	; 	' dots are plotted by VPOKEing the PATTERN table (rows 21-23 sit in the
16704               	; 	' third screen third, so every scanner pattern is at base 4096).
16705               	;
16706               	; 	' --------------------------------------------------- font colours
16707               	; 	' Chars 32-90, EIGHT bytes each. Without this the font keeps whatever
16708               	; 	' CVBasic left in the colour table, which on a green store made the HUD
16709               	; 	' unreadable.
16710               	;
16711               	; scan_col3:	' one 8-byte block per canvas row: 4 px of GREY margin, then a 3 px band of furniture GREY and a yellow floor line, per 4 px level, on dark green. The Kop and the crook are coloured PER CHARACTER at run time -- see scan_set

16827               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
16828               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16829               	; 	'
16830               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16831               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16832               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16833               	; 	'
16834               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16835               	; 	' blit is
16836               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16837               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16838               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16839               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16840               	; 	'
16841               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16842               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16843               	; 	'
16844               	; 	' template ids:
16845               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16846               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16847               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16848               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16849               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16850               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16851               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16852               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16853               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16854               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16855               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16856               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16857               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16858               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
16859               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
